subsystems.name: Low-frequency aperture array
subsystems.role: collects radio waves from a wide field of view with no moving parts.

subsystems.name: Signal transport and digitisation
subsystems.role: turns analogue voltages from every antenna into digital data.

subsystems.name: Digital beamformer
subsystems.role: combines signals from many antennas to form multiple simultaneous beams on the sky.

subsystems.name: Primary science correlator
subsystems.role: performs the standard interferometry for astronomy.

subsystems.name: Technosignature search backend
subsystems.role: runs commensally on beamformed data to detect artificial narrowband signals.

subsystems.name: Timing and control system
subsystems.role: keeps all stations synchronised and manages observations.

buildSteps.title: Choose a radio-quiet site
buildSteps.detail: Select a location far from transmitters, such as the Murchison Radio-astronomy Observatory in Western Australia for SKA-Low.

buildSteps.title: Deploy antenna stations
buildSteps.detail: Install hundreds of stations, each with hundreds of dipole antennas, spread over a wide area.

buildSteps.title: Connect stations with fibre
buildSteps.detail: Lay fibre-optic cables and power to carry digitised signals to a central processing facility.

buildSteps.title: Build the beamformer and correlator
buildSteps.detail: Install computing hardware and software that forms beams and correlates signals for astronomy.

buildSteps.title: Develop the technosignature backend
buildSteps.detail: Write and test software that taps the beamformed data stream, searches for narrowband drifting signals, and filters out interference.

buildSteps.title: Integrate commensally
buildSteps.detail: Engineer the system so the search runs alongside primary observations without degrading them.

buildSteps.title: Commission and validate
buildSteps.detail: Inject known test signals and use satellites to verify detection and rejection pipelines.

buildSteps.title: Operate and survey
buildSteps.detail: Run continuously as the telescope surveys the sky, storing and analysing candidate signals.

prerequisites.why: pathfinders such as the Murchison Widefield Array and LOFAR have proven the aperture-array approach.
needed to form many simultaneous beams from thousands of antennas.
demonstrated on other telescopes but not yet at SKA scale.
artificial signals from satellites and ground transmitters must be separated from candidates.
searching wide-band data in real time requires large compute clusters.
narrowband drift-search methods exist but need scaling to SKA data rates.

pathway.milestone: Commensal SETI on existing telescopes, such as COSMIC on the VLA and Breakthrough Listen observations
SKA-Low completes construction and begins science operations
pathway.unlocks: first commensal technosignature search on a large aperture array.

pathway.milestone: Full SKA survey operations with an integrated technosignature backend
Networked searches across radio and optical facilities
pathway.unlocks: cross-checks and real-time follow-up of candidate signals.
